definitions.gloss: sneaking a taste; nibbling; pilfering food
definitions.explanation: Secretly eating small amounts of food, especially before a meal is ready or from food that isn't meant for you.
Figuratively, trying things only partially or selectively without committing to any one thing.

examples.japanese: {料理|りょうり}{中|ちゅう}につまみ{食|ぐ}いをした。
examples.english: I snuck a taste while cooking.

examples.japanese: ケーキのつまみ{食|ぐ}いがばれて{怒|おこ}られた。
examples.english: I got scolded when I was caught sneaking bites of the cake.

examples.japanese: {子供|こども}たちが{冷蔵庫|れいぞうこ}の{中|なか}のおかずをつまみ{食|ぐ}いしていた。
examples.english: The kids were sneaking bites of the side dishes in the fridge.

examples.japanese: {知識|ちしき}のつまみ{食|ぐ}いでは{本当|ほんとう}の{力|ちから}はつかない。
examples.english: You can't develop real ability by just dabbling in knowledge.

examples.japanese: いろいろな{趣味|しゅみ}をつまみ{食|ぐ}いしているだけだ。
examples.english: I'm just dabbling in various hobbies.

examples.japanese: {情報|じょうほう}をつまみ{食|ぐ}いするのではなく、{体系的|たいけいてき}に{学|まな}ぶべきだ。
examples.english: Rather than cherry-picking information, you should study systematically.

notes:
From つまむ (to pinch/pick) + {食|く}い (eating). The image is of pinching small pieces of food and popping them in your mouth. Can be used with する as a suru-verb. The literal sense is playful and relatable, while the figurative sense carries a mildly critical tone about lacking depth or commitment.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- つまみ{食|ぐ}いする: to sneak a taste; to nibble
- つまみ{食|ぐ}いがばれる: to get caught sneaking food
- {知識|ちしき}のつまみ{食|ぐ}い: superficial sampling of knowledge
- つまみ{食|ぐ}い{程度|ていど}: only dabbling level

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {味見|あじみ}: tasting; sampling — done openly and with purpose (e.g., a cook tasting a dish); no sneaking implied
- {試食|ししょく}: food sampling — formally offered samples at a store
- {盗|ぬす}み{食|ぐ}い: stealing food — more serious than つまみ{食|ぐ}い
